solution: Voltaire. The prescribed Balbharati Std-10 History textbook states this outright in Chapter 1 (Historiography: Development in the West), section 1.4 Notable Scholars: Voltaire held that, alongside objective truth and the chronology of events, social traditions, trade, economy and agriculture were equally important in historiography, and this gave rise to the idea that understanding all aspects of human life matters for history writing - 'Thus, it is said that Voltaire was the founder of modern historiography.' The question is reproduced word-for-word from that chapter's own exercise. Rene Descartes is the scholar who insisted on critically verifying the reliability of documents; Leopold von Ranke gave the critical method of research based on original documents and influenced nineteenth-century historiography, but the textbook credits the FOUNDING of modern historiography to Voltaire; Karl Marx contributed the class-struggle interpretation of history.
